subject: Computer independent data description
notes: Rule: 'The high-half 2 octets and the low-half 2 octets of a four-octet sequence defined in the UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' and the NOTE: 'Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 2) for both). Code: one .NET char per character position; REVERSE is Array.Reverse over chars (splits the pair, as the rule requires); NationalCollation native order = code-unit order. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/cidd/p1.cob, p2.cob, p3.cob) with U+1F600 = D83D DE00: FUNCTION LENGTH(N"<U+1F600>") = 2 and LENGTH("<U+1F600>") = 2 (alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16 too); PIC N(4) VALUE N"a<U+1F600>b": (2:1)=NX"D83D", (3:1)=NX"DE00", (4:1)=N"b"; INSPECT FOR CHARACTERS = 04; MOVE N"<U+1F600>" TO PIC N(1) truncates to NX"D83D" (the lone high half); REVERSE puts DE00 at position 2; PIC N(2) round-trips the pair; PIC N(1) VALUE N"<U+1F600>" is refused COBOL0898 (§13.18.63.3 SR5 — cite.py OK — the literal is 2 positions); a record NX"D83D0041D83D" with lone high halves round-trips byte-exactly through SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL files (d8 3d 00 41 d8 3d) and BYTE-LENGTH = 6. Both halves (high and low) verified. Existing goldens cite 8.5.1.4 (2002/l1_char_national_argument_bound, 2002/l1_char_national_also_positions, 85/pb190_reverse_argument_shapes) but none places a surrogate code unit in data, so none is a covering test -> test-ref empty. Adjacent, not this rule: UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE use ToUpperInvariant, which maps a supplementary pair (e.g. U+10428->U+10400) as one character; the spec's own Annex C.2 case table lists supplementary mappings (10400,10428), so that is a §15.97/C.2 question for those rows, not a §8.5.1.4 defect. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ISO/IEC 10646 / UTF-16 national facility enters with ISO 1989:2002; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to 8.5.1.4; X3.23-1985 has no ISO/IEC 10646 coded character set, so the rule is vacuous at 85)
